# `fp-w1-q-x55` egress-allowlist freeze — dated amendment, epoch 1 → epoch 2 (2026-11-13)

Evidence class: recorded execution — internal record; not outside-verified.

This is a **dated declared-data amendment** under REQ-XB-116 (§3.5):
"the list SHALL be frozen with its digest before the first paid slot; a
later change is a dated amendment and a new epoch." It is **declared
data, never machinery** — no code path, codec, mediator, runner or
acceptance battery changed. The frozen epoch-1 datum is preserved
verbatim: this amendment is a **versioned successor record** (same
`protocol_id`, new `epoch`), never an in-place rewrite.

## Scope decision (verbatim)

Operator scope-decision **"Widen allowlist + Wc5"** — widen the frozen
`fp-w1-q-x55` allowlist for the task env images' apt bootstrap, then
re-run the O-surface re-proof in a Wc5 window. The Wc5 window itself is
a later gate's scope; this record is the data half only.

## Why (the declared-data finding)

Wc4 (R6.45d, PR #375 `48428e7d`) ran the re-proof to **completion** —
the machinery is repaired (zero cell-terminate exceptions, no
scope-mint/egress signature, `reward.txt` landed on every H-allow
cell) — but `task_lists.state` stays `blocked` because every H-allow
cell got `exclude:runner_infeasible:allowlist_gap{archive.ubuntu.com|unknown}`:
the verifier's apt bootstrap was **legitimately denied** under the
frozen allowlist (mediator `security.egress.decided{deny, not_allowed,
default_unmatched}` for `archive.ubuntu.com` / `security.ubuntu.com`).
The committed epoch-1 freeze is Debian-family (minted W1 for the W1
Debian images); the successor task env images are **Ubuntu noble**
(`alexgshaw/<task>:20251031`/`:20260430`), whose apt sources are
`archive.ubuntu.com` / `security.ubuntu.com` (and `ports.ubuntu.com`
for the non-amd64 architectures). The gap is a declared-data property
(REQ-XB-125), not a defect — the remedy is widening the list, which is
exactly this amendment.

## Delta — exactly three hosts, nothing else

Added to **both** `agent` and `verify` sets (the Q-X55 posture grants
apt hosts per phase; the env images are Ubuntu noble, so both phases'
apt bootstrap needs the Ubuntu mirrors):

| Host | Why |
|---|---|
| `archive.ubuntu.com` | Ubuntu noble archive — apt `update`/`install` |
| `security.ubuntu.com` | Ubuntu noble security pocket |
| `ports.ubuntu.com` | Ubuntu ports (non-amd64) archive — declared now so no arch-variant image hits a gap |

Unchanged: `permanent_denies` (`hub.harborframework.com`, `tbench.ai`
verbatim), `withheld` (empty), the Debian-family hosts (a widening
amendment narrows nothing), every registry grant, and the
Q-X55 no-`github.com`-in-agent-phase posture. No other host is added —
the scope is the task images' apt bootstrap only.

## Lawfulness under the freeze rule

`AllowlistFreeze::check_candidate` refuses `allowlist_changed` only for
a changed digest under an **unchanged** `protocol_id` + `epoch`. The
successor carries `epoch: 2` — a different epoch is "a dated
amendment's new freeze, not this check's refusal"
(`crates/hh-env/src/egress_allowlist.rs`); the r6_15 acceptance legs
cover both arms.

## Wc5 consumption (recorded, not executed here)

`hh-w1`'s prove path reads the freeze **file** (`cfg.freeze_file` →
`/opt/wc*/freeze.json`), never re-derives it — so the Wc5 window can
land this committed artifact verbatim, the same way the committed
`hh-harbor-pin/1` fixture lands as `/opt/wc/pin.json`. Note for that
gate: `hh-w1 freeze` mints a single `ImageFamily`'s list, so the
in-window "regenerate and compare digest" leg cannot reproduce the
union — Wc5 either carries the committed artifact (the recorded basis
here) or a family-union mint lands as machinery under that gate's own
scope. Neither is decided by this amendment.
